Why Gecko? A smaller path to the web

The ideas behind Gecko: readable content, familiar templates, and portable output.

GeckoGoStatic Sites

Why Gecko? A smaller path to the web

Gecko starts with a simple idea: a website should be easy to write, easy to understand, and easy to move. Content is Markdown, layouts are HTML, and the result is a directory of ordinary files.

Write with a light touch

Pages and posts live beside the project source. There is no database to manage and no application server to keep running after a build.

Make the markup yours

Gecko uses Go's standard HTML templates, so a shared base layout can define the document shell while page templates provide their own content. Start from the included theme, then change the markup and styles to fit your site.

Publish anywhere

Run `gecko build` and upload the generated `dist/` directory to static hosting. The output has no Gecko runtime dependency: it is HTML, stylesheets, scripts, and the assets your pages use.
